groups.title: CMS Integration
groups.question: Your marketing team writes content in a headless CMS, and published changes should appear without rebuilding the whole site. Explain how Astro uses a CMS and refreshes content.

followUps.Headless CMS with Astro: How does Astro pull CMS content into a static site?
followUps.Incremental Static Regeneration: How can CMS changes appear without a full rebuild?

evidence.text: Astro fetches content from the CMS API at build time.
Pages are generated as static HTML.
The site is fast because no CMS request happens per visit.

notEnough: Only saying Astro works with CMSes.

evidence.text: Specific pages can be server-rendered while others stay static.
Caching on the host or CDN keeps those pages fast.
Alternatively, a CMS webhook can trigger a rebuild when content is published.

groups.title: Data Fetching
groups.question: Your Astro page fetches the post, the author and related posts one after another and the build is slow. Explain how you would fetch data efficiently.

followUps.fetch() in Astro Frontmatter: Where does fetch in Astro frontmatter run?
followUps.Parallel Data Fetching with Promise.all: Why use Promise.all for independent requests?

evidence.text: It runs on the server, at build time or per request with SSR.
The request is not made from the user's browser.
API keys used there stay private.

notEnough: Only saying you can use fetch.

evidence.text: Awaiting requests one after another adds up their times.
Promise.all starts them together.
The total time becomes that of the slowest request.

groups.title: Astro Integrations
groups.question: You want to add a sitemap, an MDX setup and optimised images to your Astro site. Explain the integration system and image handling.

followUps.Official Integrations Ecosystem: What can an Astro integration do?
followUps.Image Optimization with astro:assets: What does the Image component from astro:assets do?

evidence.text: Integrations hook into Astro's build and dev server.
They can add renderers, processors and scripts.
They are added in the Astro configuration.
It generates optimised formats like WebP or AVIF.
It resizes images to the needed dimensions.
It sets width and height to prevent layout shift.

groups.title: TypeScript and API Types
groups.question: A CMS API changed a field and your pages broke silently, and every page reloads the same user from the database. Explain how you would type API data and share request data.

followUps.Typing External API Responses: How do you make API responses type-safe?

evidence.text: Interfaces describe the expected response shape.
Type assertions alone do not check the real data.
Validating with Zod catches changed or missing fields at runtime.
Astro.locals holds data for a single request.
Middleware sets it, for example with the current user.
Pages and endpoints read it without loading the data again.
